message.reasoning: We need to answer from policy excerpts. The question: "If we turn on SSO, will staff who still use a password get locked out right away, or can both methods run at the same time?" According to DOC-009 part 1: Enabling SSO does not immediately disable password sign-in for existing staff. Both methods coexist until an admin separately turns password sign-in off, in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. So answer: they can coexist; only when Require SSO is turned on will password sign-in be disabled. So we can answer.

function.arguments: {"message":"Enabling SSO doesn’t immediately lock out staff who still use passwords. Both password sign‑in and SSO can coexist until you explicitly turn on “Require SSO” in Settings → Security → SSO. Once you enable that, password sign‑in is disabled for the whole workspace."}

arguments.message: Enabling SSO doesn’t immediately lock out staff who still use passwords. Both password sign‑in and SSO can coexist until you explicitly turn on “Require SSO” in Settings → Security → SSO. Once you enable that, password sign‑in is disabled for the whole workspace.
